name: Opioid Addiction
remarks: The original models the United States opioid crisis from 1990 to 2014: directed use after a prescription, misuse, addiction, overdose, detoxification and treatment, with risks by socioeconomic category. In a Greek run it had a share of 28% of the opioid prescriptions, and with the chronic pain module 5.6% of patients had an overdose (Greece: 0.03% of deaths from drug dependence, Eurostat 2022).

The other modules (injuries, surgery, cancer pain, heart attack) give opioids for acute and terminal pain and assign them to the attribute opioid_prescription; they rely on this module to end the prescription and to clear the attribute, otherwise nobody can be prescribed an opioid a second time. This copy does only that: after the prescription it ends the medication with the original weekly chance of 23.81% (a mean of about 4 weeks) and clears the attribute. There is no date guard (the original stopped in 2014, after which the attribute was never cleared), no misuse, no addiction and no overdose.
